A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MINIF2F-DAFNY and provide readable text, equations, tables, code figures, and complete Appendices A–B. Corresponding experiments and supporting material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4 and Table 2 report original Dafny and Lean baseline evaluations and seven LLM evaluations, with generated proof examples in Appendix A.

after.justification: The original evaluations remain, supplemented by Claude Opus 4.6 results, library verification outcomes, and new ablation and overlap analyses.

M1.justification: The documented Dafny/Z3 workflow, two-stage solution validator, iterative error-feedback procedure, and Appendix B prompts are retained. The reported library proof work revises the formal trust basis without establishing a change to the proof-generation algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 488 translated miniF2F problems, mathematical domains, and problem sources. The new checks examine existing problems and their supporting library rather than extending benchmark task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Claude Opus 4.6 to the seven existing LLMs. All previous comparators, including the Dafny verifier and Lean grind, remain.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 replaces v2's statement that some models used subsets with evaluation of every model on all 244 test problems. V2's table already listed 244 throughout, so this establishes a reporting revision without establishing reruns. V3 also introduces the definitions-removal control; existing generation budgets and verifier settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 substantially expands validation beyond the retained 14-problem manual check, error analysis, and proof examples. Sections 3.3–3.4 add verification of previously axiomatized library lemmas and an empty-proof ablation removing definitions.dfy. Sections 1 and 4.1 add Dafny/grind success-overlap analysis and characterize Dafny-exclusive successes by problem family.

E5.justification: Both report four verifier attempts and up to four independent LLM trajectories. Neither version supplies seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or additional uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial validation findings: 128/160 library lemmas proved, 142/201 baseline successes retained without definitions.dfy, and 67 shared, 28 Dafny-only, and 12 grind-only successes. Table 2 adds Opus 4.6 at 58.2/61.5/62.7% pass@1/2/4, making it the best reported model. Every pre-existing table score remains unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 describes an axiomatized support library. V3 reports replacing 128 of 160 axiomatized lemmas with Dafny-checked proofs: 58 verified with empty bodies and 70 using LLM-generated proofs. This substantially revises the documented trusted assumptions. The new proof scripts are not reproduced; the displayed definitions and Appendix A proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains the first miniF2F translation to an auto-active verifier. V3 reframes the contribution around a complementary empirical setting and updates the headline result from seven models and 55.7% to eight models and 62.7% cumulative pass@4 on the full test set.

C2.justification: V2 presents successful manual proofs as evidence of soundness and semantic preservation and emphasizes stronger Dafny automation. V3 explicitly limits what the validation establishes, distinguishes the support layer from foundational mathematics, and interprets grind-exclusive successes as complementarity. The conclusion newly acknowledges Lean's substantially richer expressiveness and libraries.

D1.justification: V3 newly states that translation was human-led and human-reviewed, explains how the library proofs were obtained, and explicitly reports public availability of evaluation infrastructure. Existing prompts, validator details, Dafny version, timeout, temperature, and token limit are retained.

R1.justification: Section 5.2 adds DeepSeek-Prover-V2 and explicitly credits prior hybrid and subgoal-decomposition systems for delegating low-level proof work, locating this paper's distinction in auto-active verification. Other bibliography revisions largely correct capitalization and metadata.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites affect the abstract, introduction, support-library discussion, evaluation, and conclusion. V3 also adds a conflict-of-interest disclosure and conference publication text. The section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a model row, Figure 3 moves between columns, and Figure 6 uses smaller, more compact code typesetting. Existing figures and appendix listings are retained. Listing 4's caption is corrected from an initial-generation prompt to an error-correction prompt.

improvement.justification: V3 improves evidential support and claim calibration through the library audit, definitions-removal ablation, overlap analysis, and clearer sample-size reporting. However, Figure 4 retains inconsistent logb constraints: for 0 < b < 1 and x > 1, they require a positive result while the change-of-base equation gives a negative result. The useful additions therefore leave an important soundness problem in the displayed foundation unresolved.
